AtomicPreference.rationale: Milestone trip; couple has sworn off substandard accommodations after one bad experience.
Group travel requires verified, reliable stays to avoid logistics disasters.
University students on a pooled budget; exceeding this creates social tension over cost-splitting.
Corporate reimbursement policy caps nightly accommodation at $200.
Backpacker keeping absolute frugality for overnight stays.
Students with shared food budget; each meal must stay under $25/person.
Backpacker surviving on minimum per-meal spend to fund more accommodation nights.
Food enthusiast requires at least one top-tier culinary experience for the travel.
Group wants to avoid genuinely bad meals; 3.5 is the minimum acceptable baseline.
Photographer's entire trip purpose; at least one natural setting is non-negotiable.
One or more group members specifically came for entertainment scene.
Traveler booked trip specifically to recover from burnout; wellness visit is among the top goal.
Traveler celebrating 21st birthday and wants the classic casino experience once.
Trip is a child's school-year reward; theme park is the centerpiece they were promised.
Traveler visits cities specifically to purchase local fashion and unique regional souvenirs.
Music enthusiast traveling to catch a specific tour or festival.
Family with young child; animal encounter is the one activity the child specifically requested.
Hands-on learner wants to take a local craft or culinary class for authentic cultural engagement.
Traveling with a recovering gambler; all gambling venues are strictly avoided.
Family trip with children ages 8 and 10; both categories are legally or practically off-limits.
Limited vacation time; traveler refuses to risk any activity on a mediocre-rated venue.
Travel blog with 80K subscribers requires credibly recommendable attractions only.
Accommodation budget consumes most funds; minimal money left for transit.
Visiting a coastal/bay city or experiencing a trip from water sports is a specific bucket-list goal.
First-time visitor to city; iconic landmarks are the minimum justification for the trip.
Trip after a run of poor budget-rental stays hence would like to skip the cheapest lodging tier.
Avoiding the cheapest eateries and holding a price floor across every meal as a food-safety precaution rather than luxury choice.
Stay clear of extremely low-rated places as they are often disappointing, scammy, or of no value for time.

CompositePreference.rationale: Combines preferred cuisine with a quality floor; bad food at a preferred cuisine is still unacceptable.
Well-rated mid-range units have durable finishes that protect the security deposit.
Retired person(s) who specifically enjoy natural and historical places in a trip and finds mediocre places actively irritating; 4+ reliably filters out such attractions.
CompositePreference.raw_source: Attraction.category ∈ {Museums, Nature & Parks, Sights & Landmarks} [all] AND Attraction.rating ≥ 4 [all]

CompositePreference.rationale: Budget-authentic preference: wants real ordinary food but won't risk a genuinely bad street-food experience.
CompositePreference.raw_source: Restaurant.cuisine ∈ {Street Food, Mexican, Chinese} [all] AND Restaurant.aggregate_rating ≥ 3.5 [all]

CompositePreference.rationale: Two group members want entirely different trips; the AND combined with any scope is the negotiated group agreement.
CompositePreference.raw_source: Attraction.category ∈ {Museums, Sights & Landmarks} [any] AND Attraction.category ∈ {Nature & Parks, Outdoor Activities} [any]

CompositePreference.rationale: Cheap meal must be filling enough to carry a full day of activities; Mexican and American fast-casual deliver best value-per-calorie.
Food philosopher's principle: "No excuse for expensive AND bad; cheap AND good is a discovery."
Prefers genuine nature experiences; corporate theme parks don't count as "outdoors" philosophically.
CompositePreference.raw_source: Attraction.category in {Outdoor Activities} [any] AND Attraction.category not_in {Water & Amusement Parks} [all]
CompositePreference.notes: TODO: Clean separation between likes and dislikes; inclusion and exclusion lists can be expanded per query (cf. RealTravel pattern). Children[0] is the positive filter, children[1] is the negative filter.

CompositePreference.rationale: Light-sleeper with asthma; needs both a quiet AND smoke-free certified environment.
CompositePreference.raw_source: Accommodation.review_rate ≥ 4.0 [all] AND Accommodation.house_rules ∋ {No smoking, No parties} [all]

CompositePreference.rationale: Anniversary romantic dinner must be at least European cuisine once AND demonstrably excellent throughout.
CompositePreference.notes: TODO: Really good example of any and all combination. Cuisine list under scope='any' can serve as a query-level subset partition of the broader cuisine constraint if provided, but an be used as is if no cuisine constraint provided.

CompositePreference.rationale: Partner with fish allergy requires total seafood exclusion plus a quality floor for remaining options.

A single person definitely wants to have at least one experience of each of the stated attractions. Alternatively, two members in a group want partially different / diverging trips; the AND combined with any scope is the negotiated group agreement.
CompositePreference.raw_source: Attraction.category ∈ {Boat Tours & Water Sports} [any] AND Attraction.category ∈ {Nature & Parks} [any]
CompositePreference.notes: TODO: Category lists under scope='any' can be expanded per query to reflect richer group preference partitions (cf. taken or inspired from RealTravel likes and dislikes patterns).

CompositePreference.rationale: Have a desire to learn local craft as a new and one-off experience or visit a top-rated attraction which can at least compensate even if this is not met with a great experience.
Group philosophy: pay under $100 and adjust expectations, OR pay enough to guarantee excellence. The mid-range is worst value.
Wants relaxed leisure like arcades without the exhaustion and expense of a massive theme park.
CompositePreference.raw_source: Attraction.category ∈ {Fun & Games} [any] AND Attraction.category not_in {Water & Amusement Parks} [all]

CompositePreference.rationale: Philosophy for quality: avoid cheap diners and cheap accommodation below a reasonable value as extremely cheap are often bad and unsatisfying.
Philosophy for quality: avoid bottom-tier rated visits and cheap accommodation below a reasonable value as extremely low-rated and cheap are often bad and unsatisfying.

NumericPreference.rationale: Minimize average meal cost keeps all members financially comfortable.
Maximize average attraction quality as an indicator of post-trip satisfaction.
Cost-sensitive travel strategy that aims to keep overall accommodation spending consistently low across the trip.
Worst trip memories stem from one terrible day; maximizing the experience of least rated attraction eliminates this specific source of dissatisfaction.
Focus on consistently high-quality dining experiences, treating meals as a key part of the trip rather than a necessity, so they tend to favor restaurants that reliably deliver strong ratings.
Prioritize staying in consistently well-reviewed accommodations to ensure each stay reflects a high standard of comfort and service.
Minimize the maximum dining expense, avoiding situations where one meal feels like it disproportionately drives up the overall food budget or creates an imbalance in spending expectations.

Avoid any single transportation leg becoming disproportionately expensive, transit costs stay within a comfortable and predictable range at the top end enabling better utilization for other components.
"Splurge" dinner budgeted for a celebration with the most expensive restaurant indicating the best available experience.
Interested in staying at places with least downside and thus prefer to have the accommodation with least review score to be as high as possible.
Members resent a single bad meal so targeting the minimum to be maximized ensures even the weakest restaurant is as good as possible.

ConditionalPreference.rationale: Heavy or strenuous activities are to be balanced with relaxing activities somewhere in the itinerary so that different energy preferences and pacing are accommodated.
ConditionalPreference.raw_source: IF Attraction.category ∈ {Outdoor Activities} THEN Attraction.category ∈ {Spas & Wellness}

ConditionalPreference.rationale: If splurging on a fancy hotel, must eat economically to balance the daily budget.
Reflects two different city preferences from different group members, so both needs to be included to satisfy each traveler's primary destination interest.
ConditionalPreference.raw_source: IF Day.city = San Francisco THEN Day.city = San Diego

ConditionalPreference.rationale: In a self-driving itinerary, prefer accommodations with easier parking access, flexible check-in routines, and a more residential setup.
ConditionalPreference.raw_source: IF Transportation.mode == self-driving THEN Accommodation.room_type = Entire home/apt

ConditionalPreference.rationale: Balance a premium dining experience with affordable meal.
Inclusion of cultural/indoor learning experiences in itinerary should also be matched with having at least one outdoor immersive or thrilling activity.
ConditionalPreference.raw_source: IF Attraction.category ∈ {Museums} THEN Attraction.category ∈ {Boat Tours & Water Sports}

ConditionalPreference.rationale: Saving accommodation cost which by Shared room can be utilized for fine dining.
ConditionalPreference.raw_source: IF Accommodation.room_type = Shared room [any] THEN Restaurant.rating ≥ 4.5 [any]

ConditionalPreference.rationale: Can tolerate accommodation quality falling below the comfortable threshold (e.g., due to limited availability), but then need good rated food to balance.
Balance a premium stay experience with affordable accommodation.
Planning a casino outing means potentially carrying cash or payouts, hence would like to avoid shared room throughout the trip for security and peace of mind.
ConditionalPreference.raw_source: IF Attraction.category ∈ {Casinos & Gambling} [any] THEN Accommodation.room_type not_in [Shared room] [all]

LexicographicPreference.rationale: Would strongly prefer spicy Chinese, Mexican, and Indian food, other stated cuisines are acceptable but fallbacks.
LexicographicPreference.raw_source: Restaurant.cuisine in {Chinese, Mexican, Indian} ≻ Restaurant.cuisine in {French, Italian}

LexicographicPreference.rationale: Attractions needs to be iconic and photogenic, hence, highest preference to recognizable sights, museums and scenic nature spots, other attractions are flexible once these are covered except for high-noise events such as concerts, shows, or other nightlife venues.
LexicographicPreference.raw_source: Attraction.category in {Sights & Landmarks, Nature & Parks, Museums} [any] ≻ Attraction.category not_in {Concerts & Shows, Nightlife} [all]

LexicographicPreference.rationale: Social travelers prioritize shows/club/bar scene or socially energetic activity at least once with highest priority. Other activities are also acceptable but classes and workshops are boring though and not a fan of losing money in casinos and gambling.
LexicographicPreference.raw_source: Attraction.category in {Nightlife, Fun & Games, Concerts & Shows} [any] ≻ Attraction.category not_in {Casinos & Gambling, Classes & Workshops} [all]

LexicographicPreference.rationale: Privacy and personal space during stays is preferred, so they prioritize entire apartments or private rooms, while shared rooms are only acceptable if no private options are available.
LexicographicPreference.raw_source: Accommodation.room_type in {Entire home/apt, Private room} ≻ Accommodation.room_type = Shared room

LexicographicPreference.rationale: Values deep cultural, historical or local iconic immersions the most and hence the trip should be focused on these. Other activities are still enjoyable except for shopping, casino and gambling, or food and drink based events / attractions since they are covered explicitly through resraurants.
LexicographicPreference.raw_source: Attraction.category in {Museums, Sights & Landmarks} [any] ≻ Attraction.category not_in {Shopping, Casinos & Gambling, Food & Drink} [all]

LexicographicPreference.rationale: Quality outweighs specific cuisine preference at least for once: an exceptional restaurant of any type beats a mediocre preferred-cuisine one.
Staying in places that allow flexibility and comfort in how to use the space with regard to smoking or visitors at least once is preferred over strictly optimizing for cost.
LexicographicPreference.raw_source: Accommodation.house_rules not_in {No smoking, No parties, No visitors} [any] ≻ Accommodation.price ≤ 150 [any]

LexicographicPreference.rationale: Experience-maximizer: prefers standout, highly-rated memorable experiences over sticking to specific categories, e.g. would rather choose a truly exceptional boat tour than a mediocre museum or landmark.
LexicographicPreference.raw_source: Attraction.rating ≥ 4.5 [all] ≻ Attraction.category ∈ {Museums, Sights & Landmarks, Nature & Parks} [any]

LexicographicPreference.rationale: Keeping the whole family or group together in one shared space matters more than staying in a higher-rated accommodation with separated rooms or layouts.
Trip is centered around activities and experiences, hence prioritize visiting highly rated attractions over staying in premium accommodations that are mainly used for resting at night.
Air travel preferred as it entails less transit time, and reduces the fatigue and coordination effort associated with long road journeys via taxi or self-driving.
Having consistently comfortable accommodations throughout the trip is preferable to occasionally dining at a highly rated restaurant.
Restaurants are visited multiple times every day while accommodations are mainly used for sleeping, prioritize consistently decent dining experiences over staying in a premium hotel.

Atmosphere and social energy of the activity matter more than whether every attraction is top-rated; would rather have memorable nightlife and interactive experiences than only visit highly reviewed places.
Need to satisfy our taste buds with our favourite cuisine at least once is preferred over strictly optimizing for cost.

CompensatoryPreference.rationale: When availability forces a 3.7-rated hotel, an exceptional dinner becomes the day's qualitative anchor—hotel is where you sleep; restaurant is where memories are made.
Price flexibility is permitted precisely and only when quality is demonstrably exceptional; mediocre at any price is never justified.
Photographer values category significance over marginal rating shortfall; a 4.1-rated iconic landmark produces better photographs than a 4.8-rated escape room.
CompensatoryPreference.raw_source: PRIMARY: Attraction.rating ≥ 4.5 | MARGIN: ≥ 4.0 | SECONDARY: Attraction.category ∈ {Sights & Landmarks, Nature & Parks}

CompensatoryPreference.rationale: If the preferred cuisine isn't available, a cultural attraction compensates by making the day still feel culturally meaningful.
CompensatoryPreference.raw_source: PRIMARY: Restaurant.cuisine ∈ {Mexican} | MARGIN: cuisine ∈ {American} | SECONDARY: Attraction.category ∈ {Museums, Sights & Landmarks} [same day]

CompensatoryPreference.rationale: Self-driving day is offset by exceptional accommodation; if you must self-drive, at least the place you stay is outstanding and comfy for rest and relieve from tiredness.
CompensatoryPreference.raw_source: PRIMARY: Transportation.mode = taxi | MARGIN: self-driving | SECONDARY: Accommodation.rating ≥ 4.5 [same day]

CompensatoryPreference.rationale: A less-preferred landmark day is elevated by pairing with a dinner of preferred cuisine choices; the meal redeems the activity.
CompensatoryPreference.raw_source: PRIMARY: Attraction.category ∈ {Museums} | MARGIN: Sights & Landmarks | SECONDARY: Restaurant.cuisine ∈ {French, Italian} [same day]

CompensatoryPreference.rationale: Lower attraction quality is offset by returning to a good hotel—the accommodation quality rescues the day.
CompensatoryPreference.raw_source: PRIMARY: Attraction.rating ≥ 4.5 | MARGIN: ≥ 4.0 | SECONDARY: Accommodation.rating ≥ 4.0 [same day]

CompensatoryPreference.rationale: Lower hotel quality is offset by a spa visit; the physical wellness experience provides the comfort the hotel falls short on.
CompensatoryPreference.raw_source: PRIMARY: Accommodation.rating ≥ 4.0 | MARGIN: ≥ 3.5 | SECONDARY: Attraction.category ∈ {Spas & Wellness} [same day]

CompensatoryPreference.rationale: A less-preferred cuisine acceptable if an attraction of interest makes the day enjoyable.
CompensatoryPreference.raw_source: PRIMARY: Restaurant.cuisine ∈ {French} | MARGIN: Mediterranean | SECONDARY: Attraction.category ∈ {Museums, Sights & Landmarks} [same day]

CompensatoryPreference.rationale: Slightly lower dining quality is compensated by a high-culture day; a meaningful attraction experience makes an adequate meal feel sufficient.
CompensatoryPreference.raw_source: PRIMARY: Restaurant.aggregate_rating ≥ 4.5 | MARGIN: ≥ 4.0 | SECONDARY: Attraction.category ∈ {Museums, Sights & Landmarks} [same day]

CompensatoryPreference.rationale: Lower attraction quality compensated by preferred cuisine at dinner; the favored meal experience rescues a less-ideal sightseeing day.
CompensatoryPreference.raw_source: PRIMARY: Attraction.rating ≥ 4.5 | MARGIN: ≥ 4.0 | SECONDARY: Restaurant.cuisine ∈ {Chinese, Mexican, Mediterranean} [same day]

CompensatoryPreference.rationale: Strongly prefers excellent accommodation but will lower standards drastically if the hotel has better affordability.
Seeking perfection but will accept a great meal if it represents exceptional financial value—quality AND affordability together substitute for top-tier quality alone.
Wants live music but will go to a highly-rated nightclub as a fallback if no concert is available.
CompensatoryPreference.raw_source: PRIMARY: Attraction.category ∈ {Concerts & Shows} | MARGIN: Nightlife | SECONDARY: Attraction.rating ≥ 4.0

CompensatoryPreference.rationale: Prefer good attractions with local feel and sense of common belonging, can go for extremely highly-rated places which are often too crowded or touristy for our taste, provided we have a private accommodation space to ourselves.
CompensatoryPreference.raw_source: PRIMARY: Attraction.rating ≤ 4.5 | MARGIN: Attraction.rating ≥ 4.5 | SECONDARY: Accommodation.room_type ∈ {Entire home/apt, Private room}

always.rationale: Health enthusiast who runs in a park every day regardless of city or weather.
Keep one meal each day simple and inexpensive, especially when a traveller or some member of the group is budget focused.
Traveler refuses to waste a single day of limited vacation on mediocre experiences. At least one attraction per day should be high rated.
Food blogging during the trip, must post a high-quality meal every day; a substandard meal is a content failure.
First-time tourist determined to see an iconic monument or landmark every day of the trip.
Luxury honeymoon; one meal every single day is a splurge, no compromises for the duration.

sometime.rationale: User (RealTravel) wants at least one culturally significant museum visit per city across the whole trip.
Group has budgeted for one exceptional dining experience as a trip highlight.
Two group members specifically came for entertainment scene; at least one night out is required.
A group member recovering from surgery needs at least one physical recovery/wellness session.
User (TravelBench) needs at least one photography-worthy iconic landmark for the trip's centerpiece shot.
Anniversary couple agreed on at least one night in a home with ocean view and kitchen for a private dinner.
Group member with casual curiosity about casinos asked for one novelty visit; one-time experience needed for closure.
Trip philosophy includes at least one premium bucket-list experience that justifies a one-time splurge.
Group of sedentary desk workers agreed to include at least one active outdoor experience.
Photographer's curated collection needs one truly world-class landmark as the centerpiece shot.
Music / theater fan specifically traveled for a concert; at least one show in each city.
Souvenir obligations must be met; at least one shopping stop is required.

within.rationale: Prefer visiting a major landmark within the first two days to ensure the trip's primary sightseeing objective is met before the potential onset of travel fatigue or unexpected scheduling conflicts.
Front-loading heavy educational content while energy and focus are highest early in the trip.
Exploring the local natural landscape early in each city stay while legs are fresh.

Boat tour or water sports early after arriving in a city because it gives a relaxing introduction to the city and helps them quickly get familiar with the surroundings and main sights (in case of boat tours).
within.raw_source: within(Attraction.category ∈ {Boat Tours & Water Sports}, k=1) [scope: per_city]

within.rationale: Doing the grueling hike early in the trip when legs are fresh and energy is at its trip-highest.
Anchoring the start of each day with a major landmark ensures the core sightseeing gets done before fatigue.
Appeasing children early in the trip ensures good behavior; delaying the promised attraction creates days of nagging.
Starting with quality lodging sets the standard and prevents early bad experiences from coloring the trip.
Cultural and educational experiences are best absorbed before theme park or entertainment days lower the child's tolerance for them.
Try an anticipated cuisine (e.g. for a  younger members, children) early in the trip to maintain excitement and avoid repeated anticipation-related disappointment from the younger travelers.
Group treats the first day meal in each city as an important arrival experience and prefers a well-rated restaurant to create a strong first impression of the food scene.
Starting each day with an inexpensive meal to keep daily food spending flexible for a potentially higher-quality dinner later in the day.
Start the day with sightseeing immediately after attractions open and delaying the first meal until lunchtime as a brunch to maximize crowd-free exploration time.
Intend to host someone during the initial days hence house rules should allow that during the first stay.

atmost_once.rationale: Budget allocated for exactly one luxury dinner; a second fine-dining visit double-spends the luxury fund.
Group with recovering gambler allows at most one brief casino visit as a negotiated social compromise.
Group accepts one shared-room night if no alternative exists; two or more would constitute a pattern of quality compromise.
Two early risers in the group; one night out is the fair compromise, not multiple disrupted sleep schedules.
Child becomes unbearably overstimulated after two consecutive theme park visits; one is exciting, two creates exhaustion, meltdown, or irritability.
Social group accepts one strict accommodation restriction for a logistics reason; two or more changes the trip's character.
Designates exactly one day for souvenirs so shopping doesn't consume the entire itinerary.
Concert budget allows exactly one show per city to avoid entertainment dominating the visit.
Budget allows exactly one splurge accommodation night; luxury is an experience, not a habit.
Came to relax; one workshop satisfies the organizer's hands-on learning preference without dominating the trip.
Pragmatic wellness traveler limits spa visits to once per city to prevent wellness dominating a culturally diverse itinerary.
Traveler gets museum fatigue quickly; one visit per trip is educational, two is exhausting.
French food is too rich and heavy to eat on multiple days in a row.
Wants to be social; will only tolerate an anti-visitor rule for one quick 1-night layover.
Refuses to pay surge pricing or luxury transit fees more than once; budget integrity demands it.

sometime_before.rationale: Wants to learn the history and cultural context of local place before buying souvenirs as keepsakes.
Calm nature outings more enjoyable before accumulated travel fatigue and night activities reduce daytime energy levels or disrupt sleep schedules.
Scheduling physically active outdoor sightseeing before relaxing spa or wellness activities so the trip feels balanced and recovery-oriented.
Educational calm of zoo sets the trip's mood before the overstimulating theme park, especially for children.
sometime_before.raw_source: sometime_before(Attraction.Zoos & Aquariums, Attraction.Water & Amusement Parks) [scope: global]

sometime_before.rationale: Attends local craft workshop before shopping for crafts to distinguish quality handmade work from mass-produced tourist items.
Prioritize low-cost dining before so that occasional splurges later feel intentional and financially comfortable.
Crowd-aware traveler visits popular sights first, then ease into less crowded activities during the day's window.
sometime_before.raw_source: sometime_before(Attraction.category == Sights & Landmarks, Attraction.category != Sights & Landmarks) [scope: per_day]

sometime_before.rationale: Prefer a high-rated hotel before a low-rated one, as early low-rated stay may kill the buzz and mood itself.

sometime_after.rationale: Physical therapist's protocol: wellness treatments are therapeutically effective post-exertion; spa before activity provides no physiological benefit.
Cultural literacy precedes shopping; the museum visit provides the knowledge that transforms purchases into meaningful keepsakes.
sometime_after.raw_source: sometime_after(Attraction.category in {Museums, Sights & Landmarks}, Attraction.Shopping) [scope: global]

sometime_after.rationale: Family tests a private-room night first to see if the child manages the unfamiliar environment, transition to home rentals sometime after to provide a closed environment in a familiar set up.
Nightlife may induce morning disruptions and fatigue which needs recovery sometime after through spa and wellness attraction visit.
Hands-on learner processes cultural knowledge by visiting landmarks followed by classes and workshops as it creates expert appreciation for what's visited before.
Academic traveler needs unstructured outdoor time after cognitively dense museum visits; nature provides the decompression that integrates museum content.
Modest accommodations should be booked first to enhance the premium stay's impact; contrast creates genuine appreciation rather than entitled expectation.
Get to know the city through its outdoor activities first before engaging in commercial activity.
Saves the big monuments for the days following the stressful arrival or departure days, travelling days can be utilized for other activities.
sometime_after.raw_source: sometime_after(Day.travel_phase in {arrival, departure}, Attraction.Sights & Landmarks) [scope: per_city]

always_within.rationale: Museum visit always prompts wanting to see the relevant physical landmark the same or next day; museum-without-landmark feels incomplete.
Manage spice or texture intensity with a spicy meal always balanced by a milder cuisine.
always_within.raw_source: always_within(Restaurant.cusine in [Mexican, Indian] → Restaurant.cusine in [French, American], k=1) [scope: global]

always_within.rationale: Recovery protocol: every strenuous outdoor day must be followed within one day by a spa treatment.
always_within.raw_source: always_within(Attraction.Nature & Parks → Attraction.Spas & Wellness, k=1) [scope: global]

always_within.rationale: Self-driving can be tiring, so the group prefers to follow it with a relaxing activity like a spa within the next day to recover and unwind.
always_within.raw_source: always_within(Transportation.mode == self-driving → Attraction.category == Spas & Wellness, k=1) [scope:global]

always_within.rationale: After a night out, prefers to schedule a spa or other relaxing activity within the next day to recover and stay refreshed for the rest of the trip.
Consistent quality dining: good meal should be consistent within some consistent duration e.g. within 3 days.
Cultural consistency: cultural attractions should be preserved throughout the trip within some consistent duration e.g. 3 days.
Budget rebalancing: every expensive dining must be followed by a budget option to avoid dining cost splurging.
Casual or lighter entertainment (arcades, bowling, game centers, etc.) before moving into more energetic nightlife activities later the next day.
Scheduling a relaxing spa or wellness activity within the next day after visiting water or amusement parks to recover from physically tiring and high-energy outings.
always_within.raw_source: always_within(Attraction.Water & Amusement Parks → Attraction.Spas & Wellness, k=1) [scope:global]

always_within.rationale: Quality bounce-back so that every below-threshold restaurant must be followed by a quality meal within the next dining slot.
Cultural consistency: cultural attractions should cluster within a city visit; visiting one makes the next more coherent and contextually richer.
Quality bounce-back so that every below-threshold attraction must be followed by a quality venue within the next attraction slot.

hold_during.rationale: The trip opens by eating unfamiliar or less preferred cuisine in the first initial days while the traveler / group has energy and appetite for exploration.
Getting a visitor friend to join just for a day and hence would like to entertain their cuisine choices with which current person or group is okay.
Some interim part of the trip is reserved for adventure activities to keep the experience cohesive and avoid logistical switching e.g. gears etc.
hold_during.raw_source: hold_during(4, 5, Attraction.category ∈ {Nature & Parks, Outdoor Activities, Boats & Water Sports})

hold_during.rationale: Disciplined early spending on food allows the traveler to budget for one or two genuinely high-end dinners later in the trip without guilt or financial strain.

Initial days focus on shared quality daytime activities and controlled spending, with nightlife and casinos reserved for the end so they don't disrupt the main itinerary and can serve as end-of-trip leisure and spending.
Preferred attractions should be visited during the first days while the traveler's energy and enthusiasm are fresh; leaving them for later risks fatigue-driven underappreciation or skipping entirely.
The interior days form the experiential core of the trip; settling for mediocre attractions during peak activity days wastes the prime window when energy and mood are highest.
The middle portion of the trip prioritizes other activities and budget balancing on food, while allowing the beginning and end for more memorable dining experiences and splurging.

hold_after.rationale: After initial days of sampling and cuisine exploration; shift toward familiar, preferred cuisines for comfort and consistency in the latter part of the trip.
The first half of the trip involved any accommodation price including premium accommodations; a hard price cap in the second half rebalances the total lodging budget back toward the original target.
hold_after.notes: Pairs well with multi-city 5-day or 7-day trips as accommodation usually transitions around these marks. Can also be paired with a complementary preference to maximize accommodation cost within budget during the complementary period.

hold_after.rationale: After the initial exploratory days, concentrate exclusively on outstanding restaurants rather than explore further, treating food as a crucial experience to optimize for towards the closing days.

Towards the latter part of the trip, the travellers accumulate fatigue; only highly rated attractions are worth the energy expenditure in the second half, making a strict quality filter which can justify high-effort attractions if included.
Spend modest during the initial part of the trip and save the later days for intentional dining splurges, making food a part of the main experience toward the end.
Exclusively budget for luxury final nights as a celebratory spending towards the trip end.
Dedicate the later half of the trip entirely to relaxed pacing and low-effort attractions.
hold_after.raw_source: hold_after(3, Attraction.category in {Spa & Wellness, Shopping, Food & Drink, Sights & Landmarks})

hold_after.rationale: Plan a deliberate celebratory close to the trip with high-spend restaurants on the final day, creating a memorable bookend to the journey.

Ending the trip in quality accommodation ensures the final memories are positive, helps with the fatigue in the journey so far and doesn't get compounded with a poor lodging experience on the last few nights.

ScopedPreference.rationale: Clubs are worth visiting on weekend when crowds, music, and energy are at peak.
Dinner is the dedicated expensive meal; breakfast and lunch can be cheap, but evenings warrant investment.
Miami's bay geography makes a water tour both uniquely feasible and culturally specific to this city.
ScopedPreference.raw_source: WHEN Day.city = Miami: Attraction.category ∈ {Boat Tours & Water Sports}
ScopedPreference.notes: TODO: Materialize through city-attraction placeholders for multi-city scenarios.

ScopedPreference.rationale: Long visit hour attractions such as Museum, Nature & Parks, or Water & Amusement Parks are to be meaningfully scheduled on full stay days, not on travel days.
ScopedPreference.raw_source: WHEN Day.travel_phase = stay: Attraction.category ∈ {Museums, Nature & Parks, Water & Amusement Parks}

ScopedPreference.rationale: Mornings require fast and light food; a sit-down breakfast at a restaurant wastes precious early sightseeing hours.
ScopedPreference.raw_source: WHEN Restaurant.meal_type = breakfast: Restaurant.cuisine ∈ {Cafe, Fast Food}

ScopedPreference.rationale: Major tourist sites are dramatically less crowded on weekdays; weekday visits maximize the experience quality.
Prefer gambling experience in the city designed for it where they are a central part of the city's atmosphere and entertainment culture.
ScopedPreference.raw_source: WHEN Day.city = Las Vegas: Attraction.category ∈ {Casinos & Gambling}
ScopedPreference.notes: TODO: Materialize through city-attraction placeholders for multi-city scenarios.

ScopedPreference.rationale: Hitting retail stores on Monday avoids the weekend shopping crowds; a quieter weekday mall is a more pleasant experience.
Keep breakfast simple and low-cost, since morning meals are usually light and not worth spending heavily on compared to other meals of the day.
Group members have friends available only on weekends; visitor-permissive accommodation is required specifically on those days.
Especially focus on seafood options when visiting coastal cities, where fresh seafood is both locally available and culturally characteristic of the destination.
ScopedPreference.notes: TODO: Materialize through city-cuisine placeholders for multi-city scenarios.

ScopedPreference.rationale: Start the day with familiar and comfort food.
Reserving more elaborate, high-quality dining experiences such as French or Italian cuisine for dinner, when there is enough time to fully enjoy a slower and more relaxed meal.
ScopedPreference.raw_source: WHEN Restaurant.meal_type = dinner: Restaurant.cuisine ∈ {French, Italian} AND Restaurant.rating ≥ 4.5

ScopedPreference.rationale: For physically risky activities like water sports or river touring, the quality must be top-rated as low-rated venues create genuine safety concerns.
ScopedPreference.raw_source: WHEN Attraction.category in [Boat Tours & Water Sports]: Attraction.rating ≥ 4.5

ScopedPreference.rationale: Highly rated entire-home accommodations, since staying in a private host property requires a stronger sense of trust and reliability.
Souvenir and shopping activities at the end of the leg in each city.
Group member returning to hometown insists LA not be reduced to clichés; substantive landmarks are mandatory when in LA.
ScopedPreference.raw_source: WHEN Day.city = Los Angeles: Attraction.category ∈ {Sights & Landmarks}

ScopedPreference.rationale: Paying premium prices demands proportional quality and rating.
Highly rated seafood restaurants because freshness and food safety matter more for seafood.
Weekends are specifically reserved for live entertainment; weekday concerts or shows miss the full crowd energy.

ScopedPreference.raw_source: WHEN Attraction.category = Museums: max(Attraction.rating) via avg

ScopedPreference.rationale: Spa day requires paired healthy, clean eating to maintain the wellness environment through the entire day.
Early arrival maximizes first-day exploration; group always prefers morning departures.
ScopedPreference.raw_source: WHEN Day.city_index in {1,2}: Transportation.mode == Flight [all] AND Transportation.arrival_time ∈ {morning} [all]

ScopedPreference.rationale: Light traveller focused on attraction visits and dining. Red-eye flights overnight save one full accommodation night per leg.
ScopedPreference.raw_source: WHEN Day.city_index in {2,3}: Transportation.mode == Flight [all] AND Transportation.departure_time ∈ {night} [all]

ScopedPreference.rationale: Breakfast is a meal to economize; paying premium for morning food more than once is a value failure.
A traveler in the group with a history of fatigue-related issues (e.g., difficulty sleeping on planes) has a firm rule: no more than one red-eye or very-late departure flight per trip.
First flight should arrive early to maximize the overall trip duration.
ScopedPreference.raw_source: WHEN Transportation.mode = Flight: within(Transportation.arrival_time = morning, k=1) [scope: global]
